unit: WF4 Distil Sources registry provenance, content alignment and heading-anchored excerpting
description: Negative control: the wrong Act body arrives under the right URL with correct provenance, and the declared-phrase content check catches it.
why_it_exists: Execution 329 (a real matter): every Sources row was written with the WRONG URL against its own title and excerpt, pairwise swapped. The url was resolved as `j.url || (ctx.urls || [])[i]`; Fetch Source runs with fullResponse: true and returns only data, headers, statusCode and statusMessage, so there is never a j.url and the positional fallback always won - and ctx.urls is a legacy list built by Build Draft Context in a DIFFERENT order from the Source Registry that actually drove the fetches. The result was a citation whose link points at a different Act: fabricated authority wearing a correct-looking title. The fallback was deleted and replaced by two independent controls, n8n pairedItem provenance and a declared-phrase content check. Provenance alone is not enough for a citation: if a proxy, a redirect or a retry serves a different Act body under the right registry entry, the URL would look right and the excerpt would be wrong. Every registry entry therefore declares want phrases taken from the operative provision.
